title.en: A stream, a boat and a naughty boy

text.en: Meena floats paper boats on a stream near a bamboo bridge. A boy keeps overturning them, and Meena gets angry. But when the boy says he does not know how to make a boat, Meena chooses to teach him instead of fighting. In this chapter you will read this story, learn new words, use he and she in place of names, and use the little words in, on and under to tell where things are.

The story takes place near a stream with a bamboo bridge. Meena puts a paper boat into the water and it sails swiftly down the stream, and she is delighted. She goes on putting several boats into the stream, one after another. Then she sees a naughty boy pushing and overturning the boats.
Meena stares at the boy angrily and shouts Stop, but he does not stop. When she asks why, he says it is fun for him, and Meena replies that the boats are hers and he must stop. The boy thinks for a minute and promises not to do it again, but he says he also wants to play. He admits that he does not know how to fold paper into a boat. Meena does not run to complain. She shows him how to fold and re-fold the coloured paper. Soon both of them have boats on the stream, and both enjoy watching them sail. This tells us that helping someone is a better answer to a problem than staying angry.
Delighted means very happy. Meena was delighted when her boat sailed fast. Several means more than two but not very many. Meena made several boats. Overturning means turning something upside down, so the boat floats badly or sinks. A stream is a small narrow river. Watched means looked at carefully for some time.
We do not need to say a name again and again. We can use a small word in its place. For a girl or a woman we use she. Instead of saying Meena walked and Meena bent, we say Meena walked and she bent. For a boy or a man we use he. Instead of saying the boy jumped and the boy pulled, we say the boy jumped and he pulled. So Rani likes playing outside and she likes flying kites. Sahil has a top and he plays with it every day.
Some small words tell us where a thing is. They are called prepositions. On means resting on top of something, like a book on the shelf. In means inside something, like books in a bag or a ball in a box. Under means below something, like a ball under the table. To choose the right word, look at the picture and ask where the thing really is.
In Let us speak, you tell the story of Manish saves the ant from the pictures, in order, beginning with what happened first. In Let us write, you look at a park picture and write a few sentences using clues like children, playing, see-saw, swings, slide, enjoying and happy. The crossword has answers about toys and games, such as top, bat, ball, marble and swing. At home you can ask your elders which games they played when they were young and learn one to share with friends.

board.text: on the box → in the box → under the box

problem.en: Fill in he or she: Durga is five years old. ___ is going to school.

text.en: Durga is a girl, so we use she.

why.en: He is for a boy, she is for a girl.

text.en: The sentence becomes: She is going to school.

why.en: She takes the place of Durga.

problem.en: Choose in, on or under: The bag is ___ the chair (the bag is sitting on top of the chair).

text.en: Look at where the bag is: on the seat of the chair.
So we write: The bag is on the chair.

why.en: In would mean inside, and under would mean below.

problem.en: Put the story events in order: A. They both sail their boats. B. Meena shows him how to fold paper. C. The boy overturns the boats.

text.en: First the boy overturns the boats.
Next Meena shows him how to fold paper.
At the end they both sail boats. The order is C, B, A.

why.en: Stories have a beginning, a middle and an end.

prompt.en: Tell the story of Meena and the boy in your own words, and say what it teaches.

requiredIdeas.en: Meena put paper boats in a stream
Meena taught him to make boats
Helping is better than staying angry

points.en: Meena helped the boy by teaching him to fold paper boats.
Delighted means very happy; several means more than two.
He is used for a boy and she is used for a girl.
On means on top, in means inside, under means below.
Kindness can turn a quarrel into play.
